pullRequests.head: fix/msvc-stl-binding-equality
pullRequests.body:
Windows native builds using Clang with MSVC STL 14.51/14.52 fail in std::find with static assertion failed: unexpected size when searching input bindings or pad chords. The STL incorrectly selects a vectorized search for these larger types with defaulted equality (microsoft/STL#6294).
Give Binding an explicit constexpr noexcept comparison of the same three fields. PadChord continues to use its defaulted comparison, which delegates to Binding; both types then avoid the broken optimization. Input…

A Steam Deck player on the dev channel could not get HDR any more, even with HDR set to On in the game. Two changes caused it:

pullRequests.body:
Before: on a Steam Deck the plugins folder was writable by all (a program started from Steam may run with umask 0), so the port refused every native mod.

How: open_to_others in mod_library.cpp checks the owner first, then closes your own world-writable items. docs/port/MODS.md updated.

pullRequests.body:
Fixes T-19: rac1 crashes on Windows when a Discord screen share starts.
Before: The crash handler is a vectored handler, so it sees every first-chance fault in the process. Our handler saw it first and ended the game ("read at host address 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF").
After: The game keeps running. Real crashes are still reported.

Mods and Games read their lists and the last save again on every visit
and came in empty, so buttons, notices and Continue popped in during the
slide. They now show what they read last at once and read it again.

commits.headline: fix(rac1): run each level's own sky routine (#500)
commits.author: nickyyOO
commits.body:
On a level, the frame draw's level copy calls the level's own sky
routine. The port's C called the executable's one instead: the title's
stars. That reseeded rand() once, called it about 250 more times a
frame, wrote 256 stars to address 0, and left Novalis's clouds still.

Wrap Transition_DrawSky: on a level, call where the level's copy of
the frame draw calls (openrac_level_call, new in the runtime). NTSC and
PAL; NTSC-J and PAL v1 leave it out until checked.

commits.headline: fix(port): ignore faults other modules catch on Windows (#502)
commits.author: nickyyOO
commits.body:
* fix(port): ignore faults other modules catch on Windows

The vectored handler saw every first-chance fault in the process and ended
the game. Overlays like RivaTuner probe memory with IsBadReadPtr and catch
the fault themselves; starting a Discord screen share set this off (T-19).
Now only faults in the game's own .exe are reported at once. A fault in
another module goes on, and the unhandled filter reports it if nobody
catches it.
